main_statement.latex: \begin{theorem}\label{thm:main} There exist a finite connected two-dimensional aspherical simplicial complex $K$ and a constant $C<\infty$ with the following properties. (i) Every combinatorial edge loop of length $\ell$ in the universal cover of $K$ bounds a disk diagram with at most $C\ell$ triangular faces. (ii) The group $\pi_1K$ admits no geometric action on a proper complete $\CAT(0)$ space. In particular, $\pi_1K$ is word-hyperbolic, and no finite simplicial complex homotopy equivalent to $K$ admits a locally $\CAT(0)$ geodesic length metric inducing its given topology. Consequently, no such model admits a compatible locally $\CAT(-1)$ geodesic length metric. \end{theorem}
main_statement.paraphrase: There is a torsion-free word-hyperbolic group G (pi_1 of a finite aspherical 2-complex with linear Dehn function) that admits no proper cocompact isometric action on any proper complete CAT(0) space, of any dimension. Hence G is not a CAT(0) group and not a CAT(-1) group, answering negatively Gromov's realization question (BMS Problem H11 for CAT(-1); Stark 2025 OP 2.15; Duchesne-Simon 2026 Question W). The proof is non-constructive: K comes from a random finite presentation selected along a diagonal sequence.

definitions.metric models: geodesic length metrics inducing the given complex topology (01:4)

headline_corollaries.paraphrase: No finite complex homotopy equivalent to K carries a locally CAT(0) (hence no locally CAT(-1)) geodesic metric: a finite aspherical complex with a linear isoperimetric inequality need not have a nonpositively curved finite model (abstract).
pi_1 K is word-hyperbolic (from (i) via linear Dehn function <=> hyperbolic).

effectivity.quote: The proof is an existence argument and does not give an effective size for $K$.

lean_route_differences: Asphericity: paper uses Hurewicz + Whitehead after showing H_2 = 0 (03:620-632); Lean constructs an explicit contraction of the voltage universal cover via pi_2-obstruction cochains and prism gluing (L06), the largest dominated branch (16%).
Infinitude: paper uses Euler characteristic with the C_2 quotient (07:28-32); Lean uses a rank bound on the six-cell boundary map (L07).
Word hyperbolicity: paper cites BH III.H; Lean proves linear filling => thin => four-point (L08).
Planar separators: cited in paper; re-proved in Lean for genus-zero rotation systems (L11).

Antipodality of M_C, M_D: paper uses a semicircle/local-geodesic argument in the CAT(1) space of directions (BH II.1.4); Lean proves it algebraically in 10 lines from pairings (L02 exceptional_antipodes).
Transverse square: paper splits the parallel set (BH II.2.14); Lean uses explicit 'translates' along the axis and add_eq_of_pairings (L02 opposite_cross_sums) - no product decomposition theorem.
Displacement bound: paper 25(1+ε)/(1-ε) on squared norms; Lean M=8 on norms from marginals <= 2/|L| (L04).
Tangent cone, ultralimit space, inductive means, Chernoff, Cartan-Hadamard: all built from scratch in Lean (Mathlib lacks them).
Statement: Lean omits 2-dimensionality and the locally CAT(0) model exclusion (keeps CAT(-1)).

eureka_candidates_ranked.name: Uniform conditional test: target-independent orthogonality <h_I, v_e> <= 0 from total-variation couplings of table matches + Sturm inductive mean + six-letter displacement bound
for: It is exactly the missing uniformity that previous approaches lacked: IKN 2012 and Toyoda 2016 give fixed points only for target classes with Izeki-Nayatani invariant bounded below 1, with constants depending on the target family (01:78-85); the paper's test holds for ANY action chosen after the tables.
Not a subterm of the goal or L; it is a new kind of statement (conditional orthogonality in tangent cones uniformly over targets).
Every metric identity in Secs 5-6 is an application (path bounds, ternary test).
against: Each ingredient is cited or standard: Sturm 2003 inductive means, Gigli-Nobili concavity, barycenter of minimizer (Gromov/IN), uniform-on-extensions couplings (random graphs).
Could be viewed as a natural 'law of large numbers in CAT(0)' argument once one decides to test averages over matches.

Search (Oct 2026) found no target-uniform version.

eureka_candidates_ranked.name: Nested near-critical random model: fans sampled first, tops only over selected fans, plus square/hexagon decorations at density just below 1/2
for: Reconciles two opposing requirements (sparsity for hyperbolicity/asphericity vs. enough constraints for metric rigidity) explicitly called out at 01:95-97.
Near-critical density makes the lower bounds of P39 tight: in the limit squares become exactly flat (two-step distance sqrt2) while hyperbolicity survives because deficits α, β-7α, δ stay positive.
